newsitem.title: GUATEMALA: Guatemala suspends peace talks with leftist rebels.
newsitem.headline: Guatemala suspends peace talks with leftist rebels.

text.p: The government said on Monday it was suspending peace talks with leftist rebels planned for Tuesday, saying the recent kidnapping of a woman by a guerrilla commander violated terms of the peace process.

The move came as a surprise, given constant assurances that the government and the Guatemalan National Revolutionary Unit (URNG) would sign a definitive peace accord by December, bringing an end to Guatemala's 36-year-old civil war.

"The URNG command must present full clarifications about what happened and about their degree of responsibility. Meanwhile the negotiation meeting is suspended," Interior Minister Rodolfo Mendoza told a news conference.
The United Nations-brokered negotiations, which began in 1991, have been smooth and hopeful throughout 1996.
They gained a new momentum in March when the guerrilla announced a ceasefire and President Alvaro Arzu responded by calling a halt to army counterinsurgency actions.
Both sides were to have met in Mexico City on Tuesday to continue talks regarding the political future of the URNG.

In recent months the government has sat back as different fronts of the URNG continued to carry out propaganda actions in rural villages, major universities, and even in the main square of the capital.
But the alleged URNG link to Guatemala's epidemic of kidnappings, a crime wave which has the entire country on edge, has evoked a strong response.
"This act...represents a violation, not only of the human rights accord...but also of the bases of the negotiation process," said Mendoza.
Mendoza said police had captured a man on Oct. 19 in connection with the kidnapping 86-year-old Olga de Novella in September. Mendoza would not say how much ransom kidnappers had asked for Novella.

The man was carrying internal URNG documents and police identified him as Rafael Augusto Valdizon Nunez, known as "Commandante Isaias," leader of one of four separate guerrilla armies that make up the URNG.
Valdizon admitted he was holding Novella and negotiated his freedom in exchange for giving her up. Novella was returned safely to her family. Valdizon is at large.
